one_line: Ninth Sikh Guru, remembered as Hind ki Chadar for defending freedom of conscience in 17th‑century India.

appearance.age_look: Appears in his mid-50s, medium height, lean but sturdy build with a calm, grounded posture.
appearance.face: Oval face with a dignified, wheatish-brown complexion, straight nose, thoughtful arched brows, gentle lines at the eyes and mouth from years of travel and teaching, and a serene, introspective default expression that hints at inner resolve.
appearance.hair: Long black hair kept neatly tied and concealed under a tall white Sikh-style turban of the 17th century, wrapped simply with a soft, slightly pointed top and a narrow pale-gold cloth band at the base; no decorative crest or plume.
appearance.costume: He wears a long, straight-cut off‑white cotton kurta reaching mid-calf with side slits, over loose, slightly tapered light-cream salwar; on top a simple knee-length pale-saffron woolen chola (robe) with a wrap front and narrow fabric tie at the waist, its edges finished with a subtle thin beige border; a plain light-grey shawl of fine wool is draped over his shoulders and chest in cooler settings; his feet are in modest brown leather mojari-style shoes with softly upturned toes; he wears a single slim steel kara on his right wrist and no other visible jewellery, emphasizing ascetic simplicity.
appearance.signature: A plain, slightly curved talwar (Indian sword) with an unadorned steel hilt wrapped in dark-brown leather and a simple scabbard of brown leather with minimal brass fittings, usually carried sheathed in his left hand or hanging from a plain cloth baldric under his shawl.

ref_desc: Guru Tegh Bahadur is a mid‑50s, wheatish-brown, oval-faced Sikh with a serene expression, long hair under a tall white turban, wearing an off‑white kurta, light-cream salwar, pale-saffron chola, grey shawl, brown mojari shoes, a single steel kara, and carrying a plain curved talwar with a brown leather scabbard.
sheet_prompt: Draw a full-body anime-style character sheet of Guru Tegh Bahadur as a dignified 17th‑century Sikh spiritual leader: a mid‑50s, lean but sturdy man with a wheatish-brown oval face, calm thoughtful eyes, and a serene, introspective expression; his long hair is tied and fully covered by a tall, simply wrapped white Sikh turban with a narrow pale-gold band at the base, no plume or ornaments. He wears an off‑white cotton kurta down to mid-calf with side slits, loose light-cream salwar, and over them a knee-length pale-saffron chola (robe) that wraps in front and ties with a narrow fabric belt, edges finished in a subtle thin beige border. Add a light-grey woolen shawl draped around his shoulders and across his chest, and simple brown leather mojari-style shoes with slightly upturned toes. On his right wrist is a single slim steel kara, with no other jewellery. His signature weapon is a plain, slightly curved talwar with an unadorned steel hilt wrapped in dark-brown leather and a brown leather scabbard with minimal brass fittings, shown sheathed and held calmly in his left hand or hanging at his side by a plain cloth baldric under the shawl. Use a muted palette of off‑white, pale saffron, light cream, light grey, and brown, and present him from multiple angles (front, side, back) plus a close-up of the face and turban to emphasize consistent features and costume details.
